children: The National Labor Relations Board has dismissed a complaint accusing Tesla of trying to thwart union organizing at its Buffalo, New York, assembly plant through restrictive rules on IT use.
The board on Wednesday summarily upheld an administrative law judge's decision that nixed a complaint issued in 2024
The judge had found that Tesla's IT policies, including barring workers from having phones, validly protected confidential information

The union argued to the NLRB that the judge should have applied a Biden-era test making it easier to challenge workplace rules instead of a more business-friendly standard from President Donald Trump's first term
Wednesday's panel included David Prouty, the board's lone Democratic member
Tesla has faced a series of NLRB complaints but has beaten several of them, including claims that union supporters at the Buffalo plant were unlawfully fired
The case is Tesla Inc, National Labor Relations Board, No. 03–CA–312352.
For Tesla: David Broderdorf of Morgan Lewis & Bockius
For the NLRB general counsel: Sarah Crowley
For the union: Ian Hayes of Hayes Dolce
